newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish depos rise but trade balanced, zloty flat.
newsitem.headline: Polish depos rise but trade balanced, zloty flat.

text.p: Polish overnight deposit rates inched up half a point on Monday as some banks needed cash to fill gaps on required monthly reserve accounts, dealers said.

Overnight rates closed at 19.40/20.60 percent, up from Friday's 18.80/20.10 percent but dealers said strong resistance was felt at around 21 percent -- a sign that some banks were looking to place cash on Monday.

"Trade was basically balanced and O/N rates hovered around 20 percent, but end-of-the-month reserve adjustments are likely to keep rates around present levels for the rest of the week," said Renata Krajewska of PKO BP.
Tomorrow/next rates closed at 19.8/20.15 percent against Friday's close at 19.2/20.2 percent.

At today's 500 million zloty primary T-bill auction the average yield of the benchmark 52-week bill eased 0.02 point to 19.44 percent and the average yield of the 8-week paper tumbled to 18.18 percent from 18.65 percent on August 26.
Dealers said that a large number of non-banking sector bids caused the fall in Poland's shortest T-bill.
The zloty closed virtually flat from Friday at 1.78/1.73 percent from the trading band centre after calmly drifting sideways during the entire trading session.
The zloty closed at 2.7930/40 to the dollar, unchanged from Friday, and at 1.8416/26 to the mark hardly changed from Friday's close at 1.8410/25.

Dealers said the zloty could weaken against the dollar if President Boris Yeltsin's upcoming heart surgery fails to restore him as Russia's leader, as investors flock to the security of the U.S. currency during periods of international uncertainty.
Yeltsin is due to undergo a bypass operation within two months time.
